domain: Indirect tax on new-build homes and on letting

rules.statement: The first delivery of a new dwelling in mainland Spain and the Balearics is subject to 10 percent IVA, including up to two parking spaces and annexes transferred together.

source.name: AEAT sede electronica
source.ref: art. 91.Uno.1.7 Ley 37/1992, Tipos impositivos en el IVA 2026

rules.statement: Viviendas de proteccion oficial of regimen especial or promocion publica, delivered by the promoter, take 4 percent IVA.
rules.notes: Not every price-limited dwelling qualifies. Only regimen especial or promocion publica. Other protected housing takes 10 percent.

rules.statement: A new-build home in the Canary Islands is subject to IGIC, not IVA. The Canaries sit outside the EU VAT territory. General rate 7 percent; 5 percent where it will be the buyer's main residence; 3 percent for qualifying categories; 0 percent for VPO of regimen general.

source.name: Agencia Tributaria Canaria
source.ref: art. 58 Ley 4/2012 as amended by Ley 4/2018

rules.notes: CRITICAL for our audience: the 5 and 3 percent rates require vivienda habitual. A non-resident buying a Canary holiday home pays the 7 percent general rate. This is often labelled 'VAT 7 percent'. The rate is right, the label is wrong, and a reader searching for Canary VAT will find nothing. Ley 9/2025 (Canary 2026 budget) did not change the general rate; it widened reduced-rate income limits and raised the reduced-rate age threshold from 35 to 40.

rules.statement: Ceuta and Melilla are outside the IVA territory and apply IPSI instead.
rules.notes: IPSI rates on new builds not obtained. Treat as unverified.

rules.statement: Residential letting is exempt from IVA. Where the landlord provides hotel-type complementary services the let is taxed at 10 percent. 21 percent applies where the operation is neither an exempt residential let nor a hotel-type accommodation service.
rules.notes: Hotel-type services means reception, cleaning during the stay, linen changes, restaurant, laundry and similar. No enacted Spanish change to short-term let VAT has taken effect; the much-discussed 21 percent on tourist lets remains a proposal. Do not code the speculative line that appears in much of the available guidance.
